title: Fundamentals of Accounting
description: Accounting for the people who run storage sites, in storage words: the equation and the accounts, debits and credits, cash and accrual, how rent and fees are earned, receivables and bad debt, fixed assets and depreciation, payables and company cards, bills and aging, the bank reconciliation, the close and the three statements, budgets, controls and the audit, and the tax paperwork that starts at a site. For managers and the accounting team's new hires.
overview: Why the numbers matter, and how any figure opens to its lines and its entry
The accounting equation and the five kinds of account
Debits and credits, with storage transactions worked
Cash and accrual, matching and the adjusting entries
Revenue at a storage company, and why lien sale proceeds are not revenue
Receivables, Aged Receivables, the allowance and the write-off
Fixed assets, depreciation and the register
Payables, the three-way match, coding and company card duties
Bills, payment terms and the payables aging
The close and the balance sheet, income statement and cash flow statement
Budgets, variance comments, internal controls and the audit
What Accounting needs from you: W-9s, sales and use tax, property tax notices
The whole course on one page

questions.q: Your area manager asks whether Temecula made money in October. Which statement do you open?
options: The income statement, which covers a period
The cash flow statement for October
questions.explanation: Did we make money is a period question, answered by the income statement. The balance sheet is one moment; the cash flow statement says where cash went.

questions.q: A tenant pays December's rent on 11/28. Where does it sit in the November books?
questions.explanation: Nothing is earned until December arrives, so the company owes the tenant a month of storage: prepaid rent, a liability. It becomes revenue on 12/01.

questions.q: A new tenant hands over a $100 security deposit with the first month's rent. What is the $100 to the company?
options: A reduction of first month's rent
questions.explanation: A security deposit is held and owed back when the tenant leaves, so it is a liability. Calling it revenue is the common mistake.

questions.q: You open a ledger line: Repairs debited $640, Accounts Payable credited $640. What happened?
options: Work was done and the company owes the vendor; the bill is unpaid
Cash came in from a vendor for a refund
questions.explanation: Debit increases an expense; credit increases a liability. The expense was recorded and the company owes the vendor. Payment would credit cash.

questions.q: Accounting pays a gate invoice that was recorded two weeks ago. Which accounts move today?
questions.explanation: The expense was recorded when the work was done. Paying clears the payable (debit) and reduces cash (credit). Expensing it again would count it twice.

questions.q: A repair is done in October and paid in November. On the accrual books, which month carries the expense?
options: October, when the work was done, paid or not
Whichever month the bill is dated
questions.explanation: Accrual counts an expense when it is incurred. Paying in November only clears the payable.

questions.q: It is month end. Which of these are adjusting entries? Pick all that apply.
options: A tenant's card payment taken at the desk
questions.explanation: A card payment is an everyday transaction. The others move revenue or expense into the right period at month end.

questions.q: Utilities doubled in November; the lines show October's late bill plus November's. That is a timing variance that reverses on its own.
questions.explanation: Two months of bills in one month is timing: December will look normal again. Three separate repair calls, by contrast, would be real.

questions.q: Valley Center is full, yet rental income dipped. The lines show two free first months on new garages. Which rent figure fell?
questions.explanation: Concessions are the gap between billed and earned rent. The site is full, so billed rent held; earned rent, which the income statement reports, fell.

questions.q: A lien sale brings in $1,500 on a unit whose tenant owed $1,200. How is the sale recorded?
options: $1,200 to the balance; $300 held for the tenant
$1,200 of rent income and $300 of fees
questions.explanation: Proceeds settle the balance owed, which was already counted as revenue when billed. The $300 surplus is the tenant's, a liability handled per state law. A lien sale is not a profit center.

questions.q: A unit renting at $150 is rented on the 21st of a 30-day month. How much prorated rent is earned this month?
questions.explanation: Ten days of a 30-day month is a third: $150 x 10/30 = $50, earned over those ten days.

questions.q: Receivables are $90,000 and the allowance is $9,000. What does the balance sheet show the company expects to collect?
questions.explanation: The allowance is a contra asset that nets against receivables: $90,000 less $9,000.

questions.q: A balance is written off after the lien process. What new expense is recorded at write-off?
questions.explanation: The write-off clears the receivable against the allowance. The expense was recorded when the allowance was built.

questions.q: A $3,800 gate operator with a ten-year life goes into service. About how much depreciation hits each month?
questions.explanation: Straight line: $3,800 over 120 months is $31.67. $380 is the yearly figure, a common slip.

questions.q: Accounting emails: an invoice for 'gate repair, Temecula' cannot be matched. What fixes it fastest?
options: Send them the ticket number so they can match it to the quote
Ask the vendor to resend it
Approve it in your reply to Accounting
questions.explanation: The three-way match needs to find what was ordered and received. The ticket number links the invoice to the approved scope, the inspection and the photo.

questions.q: A vendor's invoice dated 10/20 on Net 30 terms is already late when the vendor calls on 11/10.
questions.explanation: Net 30 from 10/20 is due 11/19, so on 11/10 it is not late yet. Check the terms on the vendor's Details tab before calling it overdue.

questions.q: At month end the books show $48,200 and the bank $47,915. A $1,120 deposit is in transit and a $1,020 check is uncashed. What is the adjusted bank balance?
questions.explanation: $47,915 + $1,120 - $1,020 = $48,015. The books then need the $185 the bank knows about and they do not, such as a returned payment.

lessons.title: Words to Know
lessons.summary: The accounting words of this course, with the rest of the Academy's, in one glossary.

questions.q: A figure on a Nexus Accounting report comes from the same Intacct books Accounting keeps, not from a second set.
questions.explanation: Greens keeps one set of books, in Intacct. Nexus Accounting reads it; it never keeps a second set.

questions.q: A manager doubts the repairs figure on her site's Income Statement in Nexus. What is the quickest way to check it?
options: Click it to see the ledger lines behind it
questions.explanation: Every amount opens the ledger lines behind it, and every line opens its entry. Rebuilding by hand is slow and misses what was posted.

questions.q: A site was profitable in March but its bank balance fell. Which statement explains where the cash went?
questions.explanation: Profit and cash differ. The cash flow statement explains the change in cash: perhaps a repave under investing or a loan payment under financing.

questions.q: Which of these is a liability for a storage company?
options: The new gate operator on the lot
questions.explanation: A deposit is owed back to the tenant. Rent owed and prepaid insurance are assets; the operator is a fixed asset.

questions.q: The office buys $40 of printer paper on the card. Which kind of account does it hit?
questions.explanation: Paper is used up this period, so it is an office supplies expense. Small purchases are expensed whatever they are.

questions.q: You see an account numbered 4210 on a report. Under the usual numbering, what kind is it most likely?
questions.explanation: The common convention runs 1000s assets, 2000s liabilities, 3000s equity, 4000s revenue, 5000s and up expenses.

questions.q: Which of these accounts grows on the credit side?
questions.explanation: Credit increases liabilities, equity and revenue. Cash, receivables and expenses grow on the debit side.

questions.q: A $20 late fee posts to a delinquent tenant. Which entry is right?
options: Debit receivables, credit late fee income
Debit cash, credit late fee income
Debit bad debt expense, credit tenant receivables
questions.explanation: The tenant owes it (an asset up, debit) and the fee was earned (revenue up, credit). No cash moved yet.

questions.q: Wages are worked in the last week of October and paid on 11/07. What is recorded in October?
options: Wages expense and a credit to accrued payroll
A prepaid wages asset for November
questions.explanation: The expense belongs to the period the hours were worked; the liability (accrued payroll) clears on payday.

questions.q: A debit to the cash account means cash went out of the bank.
questions.explanation: Debit increases an asset, so a debit to cash is cash coming in. A credit to cash is cash going out.

questions.q: Under the cash basis, a gate repair done in October and paid in November counts in which month?
questions.explanation: Cash basis counts when money moves. Accrual would put it in October, when the work was done.

questions.q: Greens pays a $12,000 insurance premium in January for the calendar year. On the accrual books, what is March's insurance expense?
questions.explanation: The premium is a prepaid asset used up a twelfth a month: $1,000. $3,000 would be the year to date through March.

questions.q: In October a site bills $60,000 of rent, collects $52,000 of it, and takes $4,000 early for November. What is October's accrual rent revenue?
questions.explanation: Accrual counts rent in the month of storage: the $60,000 billed for October. $56,000 is what the cash basis would show.

questions.q: Repairs ran $3,000 over in November. The lines show three separate gate calls. What do you write?
questions.explanation: Three separate calls are real activity. Timing is a bill in the wrong month that reverses next month.

questions.q: A tenant asks why her third-party insurance payment is not in Greens' revenue. What is true?
options: It is protection plan revenue for the site
It is revenue at year end
questions.explanation: Third-party insurance is the insurer's revenue. Collected with rent, it is a liability until remitted.

questions.q: A site's lien sale brings in $800 against a tenant balance of $1,100. How much of the $800 is revenue?
questions.explanation: Proceeds settle the balance owed, whose rent and fees were already counted as revenue when billed. The $300 still owed is written off or pursued.

questions.q: An admin fee is charged at a move-in on 11/14. When is it earned?
options: On the 1st of the next month
questions.explanation: A one-time move-in fee is earned on the day of move-in, unlike rent, which is earned over its month.

questions.q: A manager waives a $20 late fee for a long-time tenant. How should it land in the books?
options: As a marketing expense for the site
questions.explanation: A waiver reduces the revenue it waives, with the reason recorded. It is never an expense and never hidden.

questions.q: On Aged Receivables, most of your site's balance has moved into the 91-120 Days column. What does that usually mean?
questions.explanation: Old columns hold tenants deep in the delinquency process. Growth there usually means steps are late; the site works the list.

questions.q: A former tenant pays $300 on a balance written off last year. How is it recorded?
questions.explanation: Money on a written-off balance comes back as a recovery, never as new rent.

questions.q: Which site habits keep the aging short? Pick all that apply.
questions.explanation: These collect rent and move defaults through the process. Waiving fees freely cuts revenue without collecting anything.

questions.q: Bad debt expense rose this quarter. Who sets it, in practice?
questions.explanation: Accounting estimates the allowance from the aging, but the aging is set by the site's collection habits.

questions.q: A property's land is never depreciated, though the building on it is.
questions.explanation: Land does not wear out, so it is never depreciated. The building wears out and is depreciated over its life.

questions.q: A roofer replaces two damaged panels on a building. How is it usually treated?
options: A prepaid asset for the year
questions.explanation: Two panels keep the roof working as it was: a repair. Replacing every panel would add life and be capital.

questions.q: A canopy row is half built at month end. Where do its costs sit?
questions.explanation: Project costs wait in construction in progress and start depreciating only when placed in service.

questions.q: A canopy row cost $120,000; $48,000 of depreciation has been taken. What is its net book value?
questions.explanation: Net book value is cost less accumulated depreciation: $120,000 - $48,000.

questions.q: A storm destroys a canopy row. What happens in the books?
options: Its book value is written off
questions.explanation: The remaining net book value is written off as a loss; the insurance recovery is recorded against it when it comes.

questions.q: A Murrieta purchase is coded to Fairfield's entity. What goes wrong?
questions.explanation: Coding puts the cost on a site. The company total is right, but both sites' reports are wrong.

questions.q: You buy padlocks on your company card. What do you owe on the charge? Pick all that apply.
options: A memo saying what and why
questions.explanation: Receipt, memo, coding and timeliness are the card duties. A W-9 is for vendors paid for services through payables, not a store purchase.

questions.q: The gate vendor offers a discount if you pay their invoice on your card today. What do you do?
questions.explanation: A card is never how a vendor is paid for work. The invoice goes through payables and the three-way match.

questions.q: Before paying a gate invoice, what three things does Accounting match?
options: The quote, the vendor's W-9, the check
The ticket, the budget, the bank
The vendor, the manager, the auditor
questions.explanation: Ordered (approved scope and quote or a PO), received (inspection and photo or receiving note) and billed (the invoice). Classically: PO, receiving report, invoice.

questions.q: The person who takes payments at the desk also reconciles the bank. What is the problem?
questions.explanation: One person who can take and check the same cash can also hide a loss. The reconciler must be independent of the cash.

questions.q: A vendor calls on 12/05 about an unpaid invoice dated 10/20 on Net 30 terms. What is the likely cause?
options: It is stuck on a match or approval
questions.explanation: Due 11/19, so it is past due. A bill stuck in the older columns usually lacks a match, an approval or finished work.

questions.q: Where in Nexus do you see a vendor's payment terms and the bills posted against it?
questions.explanation: Accounting > Records > Vendors opens the record: terms under Billing on Details, bills and payments on Ledger Lines.

questions.q: Which report sorts what tenants owe by how long it has been unpaid?
options: Spend by Vendor for the period
questions.explanation: Aged Receivables, under Operations > Reports, reads Cubby's balances into 0-30 to 120+ Days columns. The payables aging is what Greens owes.

questions.q: Entering a vendor bill in Intacct records the expense and the payable before anything is paid.
questions.explanation: The bill records the expense (or asset) and the payable. Payment later clears the payable against cash.

questions.q: The reconciliation shows a $185 tenant card payment the bank returned. What does the site do?
options: Call the tenant; it is owed
questions.explanation: The payment bounced, so the balance reopens in Cubby and the desk works it like any unpaid rent.

questions.q: Book balance $30,400. The bank charged a $35 fee and returned a $210 payment the books do not show. What is the adjusted book balance?
questions.explanation: Bank items the books missed come off the book side: $30,400 - $35 - $210 = $30,155.

questions.q: Where in Nexus does a manager see which bank and card accounts have been reconciled?
questions.explanation: Accounting > Dashboard > Close carries the Account Reconciliations card, with each account's status.

questions.q: A charge on the bank statement that nobody recognizes can wait until next month's reconciliation.
questions.explanation: An unknown charge may be fraud: it is a same-day call, and the card is locked if nobody made it.

questions.q: Revenue was flat and repairs rose. Which line on the income statement did the manager's month move?
options: Retained earnings on the balance sheet
questions.explanation: NOI is revenue less operating expenses, the line a manager controls. Interest and depreciation do not move with operations.

questions.q: A site has $80,000 of revenue and $36,000 of operating expenses. What is its NOI margin?
questions.explanation: NOI is $44,000; divided by $80,000 revenue is 55%. 45% is the expense ratio.

questions.q: A site repaves its lot in June. Where does the payment show on the cash flow statement?
questions.explanation: Spending on long-lived assets is investing. That is how a profitable month can still leave less cash.

questions.q: Why is depreciation added back on the cash flow statement?
options: It was an expense that moved no cash
It is paid at year end
The auditor requires it on every cash flow statement
questions.explanation: Depreciation reduced net income but no cash left the bank, so the operating section adds it back.

questions.q: Your owner's review asks about October on 11/02, before the close. What do you say?
options: Use the bank balance as of 10/31 instead
questions.explanation: Late bills, depreciation, the allowance and accruals land during the close. Before it, a month is not finished.

questions.q: Earned rent is $54,000 and gross potential rent is $60,000. What is economic occupancy?
questions.explanation: Economic occupancy is earned rent divided by gross potential rent: $54,000 / $60,000.

questions.q: Which variance comment will save your area manager a follow-up question?
options: Utilities $900 over: late October bill; timing
Repairs were higher than usual this month, will watch
questions.explanation: A useful comment says what moved, why, and timing or real, from the drill-down.

questions.q: Rental income came in $1,200 over budget. How is that variance described?
questions.explanation: More revenue than planned is favorable; more expense than planned is unfavorable.

questions.q: An auditor picks one of your repair invoices. What will they do with it?
options: Follow its trail to the ticket and photo
Call the vendor to confirm the price
questions.explanation: Auditors test samples: they follow the trail from invoice to ticket to approval to photo, and test that controls happened.

questions.q: Old tickets and incident forms can be cleaned out once the year is audited.
questions.explanation: Retention is long and set by law and policy. Nothing on the records list is ever cleaned up.

questions.q: A new pest vendor finished its first job and wants to be paid. Which paper must Accounting have first?
questions.explanation: No first payment without a W-9: it gives the TIN Accounting needs to file the vendor's 1099 later.

questions.q: A county assessment notice for your property arrives in today's mail. What do you do?
options: Send every page to Accounting today
Appeal it yourself before the deadline passes
questions.explanation: Assessment notices carry short appeal deadlines. Forward every page the day it arrives; Accounting decides what to do.

questions.q: You buy disc locks online and no sales tax was charged. What helps Accounting settle use tax?
options: A memo: what it is and which property
Paying the tax on your card
questions.explanation: Whether use tax is owed depends on what was bought and where it is used. The memo and the entity coding give Accounting both.

questions.q: Sales tax collected on merchandise at the counter is revenue for the site.
questions.explanation: It is the customer's money passing through to the state: a liability until remitted.

questions.q: On the job aid, every item the site owes Accounting is something done at the time, not saved up for month end.
questions.explanation: Ticket numbers, receipts, reasons, W-9s and tax notices all happen when the event happens; same-day answers keep the close short.

questions.q: Using the job aid's steps for reading a month, what comes right after clicking the figure?
options: Read NOI and the line that moved
questions.explanation: Wait for the close, read the line that moved, click the figure, decide timing or real, then write the comment.

questions.q: A coworker says the allowance is 'money set aside in the bank.' Which is the better description?
options: Part of equity kept for losses on tenants
questions.explanation: The allowance is an estimate that nets receivables down to what will be collected. No cash is set aside.
